attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, written in his voice.

semantics.note: The normalised proposition keeps the causal part about AI making the manipulators stronger. It drops the claim that algorithmic manipulation has replaced audience interest as the cause of virality. The contract puts that claim back, but the proposition is narrower than the statement.

contract.note: The statement is firm and the plain reading is ordinary: AI made manipulation more effective, and that manipulation replaced audience interest as the driver of virality. Requiring with/without-AI comparisons is demanding but fair. The undefined terms leave the result dependent on interpretation.

evidence.note: Pre-publication investigation (Feb 2024) shows apparently AI-made TikTok videos getting millions of views. It does not separate algorithm manipulation from audience interest or measure what AI added, so it cannot support the causal claim.

OpenAI's own report, May 2024, after publication. It says the operations it studied gained little authentic engagement. That covers a different period and population, so it can caution but not contradict the claim as of March 2024.

reviews.rationale: Neither item isolates an AI-caused rise in successful recommendation manipulation, or shows audience interest being displaced. e1 shows AI content reaching people but not why. e2 is later and covers covert influence operations only. The packet does not settle the causal claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'Will' is unhedged, so this is a scored forecast. 'At some point' sets no deadline. The proposition captures portals generating answers from their own data in place of sending users to human-made sources.

contract.note: Reading 'rather than linking' as answers that make a source visit unnecessary, without requiring links to disappear, is an ordinary and fair reading. A stricter no-links reading could change the result, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Google's own announcement (May 20, 2025) of a public US rollout of AI Mode, which answers questions inside Search and allows follow-ups. It is a company disclosure, but it is a primary product announcement, which the contract accepts. Links are kept, but under the contract that does not count against the claim.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met: in May 2025 a major search portal publicly rolled out a direct-answer experience built on retrieved information, with answers given inside the portal. Links are retained, which matters only under a stricter reading than the contract's fair plain reading.
